media.title: Building the Gazebo
media.content:
Building the Gazebo

The village elders decided to build a shared grass-thatched gazebo near the main meeting square. Men brought long eucalyptus poles from the forest, while women harvested dry elephant grass from the swamp. Together, they tied the poles with strong fibers and laid the thick thatch to keep out the rain. Children carried cups of cold water to the working adults throughout the hot afternoon. In just two days, the gazebo was complete, providing a shady place for community discussions.
